value.description: The article states that Internet user-search systems predate the Web and dates WHOIS search to 1982.
The article dates an early multi-network user-search service to 1989.

value.name: Archie
value.significance: Searchable database of filenames from public anonymous FTP sites.

value.name: Gopher
value.significance: Gopher's menus led to search tools such as Veronica and Jughead.

value.name: W3Catalog
value.significance: Early web search tool based on mirroring and standardizing manually maintained resource lists.

value.name: World Wide Web Wanderer and Wandex
value.significance: A web robot and index initially used to measure the size of the Web.

value.name: ALIWEB
value.significance: Relied on site administrators to submit index files instead of using a web robot.

value.name: JumpStation
value.significance: Combined crawling, indexing, and searching in one web resource-discovery tool.

value.name: WebCrawler
value.significance: Among the first crawler-based engines to search the full text of web pages.

value.name: Lycos
value.significance: Launched from work at Carnegie Mellon University and became a major commercial endeavor.

value.name: Yahoo! Search
value.significance: Search was added to Yahoo!'s human-curated directory.

value.name: RankDex
value.significance: Used hyperlinks to assess website quality.

value.name: Netscape search distribution deal
value.significance: Netscape rotated five major search providers on its search page under commercial agreements.

value.name: Google Search and PageRank
value.significance: Google launched and later rose to prominence through ranking and interface choices.

value.name: MSN Search
value.significance: Initially relied on third-party results before Microsoft moved toward its own search technology.

value.name: Baidu
value.significance: Launched using technology associated with Robin Li's work.

value.name: Google becomes dominant
value.significance: The article attributes this to ranking quality, link analysis, and a minimalist interface.

value.name: Yahoo! search technology consolidation
value.significance: Yahoo! acquired Inktomi in 2002 and Overture-owned search assets in 2003, then launched its own technology in 2004.

value.name: Microsoft transitions to its own search technology
value.significance: Microsoft moved toward its own crawler and search infrastructure.

value.name: Bing launches
value.significance: Microsoft rebranded Live Search as Bing.

value.name: Yahoo!-Microsoft search agreement finalized
value.significance: Yahoo! Search was to be powered by Bing technology.

value.name: YaCy
value.significance: A peer-to-peer search engine listed in the article's timeline.

value.name: Qwant, Swisscows, Kagi and others appear in timeline
value.significance: The article's timeline records continuing diversity in search providers.

value.name: Brave Search and You.com
value.significance: Newer search services appear in the article's chronology.

value.name: Perplexity
value.significance: The article lists Perplexity as an AI-era search product.

value.name: AI-powered search integration
value.significance: Search increasingly combines indexing with language models for conversational answers, summaries, and contextual recommendations.

value.name: Archie
value.details: Downloaded public anonymous FTP directory listings and indexed filenames, not the contents of the files.

value.name: Veronica
value.details: Keyword search over Gopher menu titles.

value.name: Jughead
value.details: Retrieved menu information from specific Gopher servers.

value.name: W3Catalog
value.details: Standardized mirrored pages of manually maintained web resource catalogs.

value.name: World Wide Web Wanderer
value.details: Captured URLs; the article notes that URLs alone often did not provide descriptive information useful for searchers.

value.name: ALIWEB
value.details: Depended on webmasters to submit index files in a specified format.

value.name: JumpStation
value.details: Combined a crawler, index, and query interface but initially had limited fields available for indexing.
